text:
Christian Dvorak is doing the Flyers' heavy lifting and getting very little credit for it. He plays 17.88 minutes a night, up about two minutes over the last ten games, and Evolving-Hockey had his competition in the 97th percentile last season. That's the job: center the line that sees the other team's best.

The trouble is the job is going badly at 5v5. Philadelphia gets 39.5 percent of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and his three goals and seven points in 18 games sit under his projection's pace. His own chances are thin too, 0.51 expected goals per 60 against a 0.93 rate last season. Nothing here is bad luck: his shooting is right at league average and his finishing matches his chances.

What to watch: whether the reunion with Travis Konecny and Trevor Zegras that the Flyers' lines report mentioned changes the shape of his nights. Our range still has him around 46 points, which assumes the chances come back.
headline: Dvorak gets the hard minutes, not the points
